claims.source: From E16.5 to postnatal day 10 (P10), progenitors continuously, migrated, occupied, and divided in multiple outer niches including the DMS, the fimbriodentate junction (FDJ), the subpial neurogenic zone (SPNZ), the hilus (Hi), and the subgranular zone (SGZ) (Figure 1A; Altman and Bayer, 1990a; Angevine, 1965; Hodge et al., 2013; Li et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by the authors' data across multiple time points and citations to previous work.

claims.claim: By E16.5, multiple outer niches (DMS/FDJ/SPNZ/SGZ) were distinguished by IP GFP reporter mice.
claims.source: By E16.5, multiple outer niches (DMS/FDJ/SPNZ/SGZ) were distinguished by IP GFP reporter mice, in this case the knockin EomesGFP/+ line (Arnold et al., 2009), simplified to Tbr2GFP (KI) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-B), including abundant mitotic Tbr2+ IPs and Sox9+ NSCs (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: Supported by imaging data from Tbr2GFP reporter mice shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-B and Figure 1E.

claims.claim: The nascent SGZ at E16.5 was marked by horizontally aligned Tbr2+/Tbr2GFP+ IPs, located just beneath the row of Prox1+ GNs in the newly forming suprapyramidal blade (SPB) of the GCL.
claims.source: The nascent SGZ was marked on E16.5 by the presence of horizontally aligned Tbr2+/Tbr2GFP+ IPs, located just beneath the row of Prox1+ GNs in the newly forming suprapyramidal blade (SPB) of the GCL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-B).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-B.

claims.claim: By E18.5, the expanding SPB was surrounded by multiple contiguous outer niches (DMS, FDJ, SPNZ, Hi, SGZ).
claims.source: By E18.5, the expanding SPB was surrounded by multiple contiguous outer niches (DMS, FDJ, SPNZ, Hi, SGZ) (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claims.claim: NSCs and IPs at E18.5 were located in the overlying SPNZ and appeared to migrate through the nascent SPB, with some accumulating in the nascent SGZ.
claims.source: While NSCs and IPs were located in the overlying SPNZ and appeared to migrate through the nascent SPB, some had accumulated in the nascent SGZ (Figure 1F,G).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1F, G.

claims.claim: Many NSCs in the SPNZ and SGZ at E18.5 were Sox9+/PCNA+, while some were Sox9+/PCNA-, indicating a quiescent NSC state.
claims.source: Co-labeling of Sox9+ NSCs with PCNA, a marker of proliferating cells, showed many NSCs in the SPNZ and SGZ were Sox9+/PCNA+, while some were Sox9+/PCNA-, indicating a quiescent NSC state, especially along the SGZ (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Many Nestin- and/or GFAP-labeled glial processes (and some mitotic figures) were aligned along the DMS at E18.5, but radial processes uniformly spanning the SPB were not yet apparent.
claims.source: While many Nestin- and/or GFAP-labeled glial processes (and some mitotic figures) were aligned along the DMS, radial processes uniformly spanning the SPB were not yet apparent (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claims.claim: By postnatal day 2 (P2), at the peak of GN neurogenesis, the infrapyramidal blade (IPB) of the GCL had begun to form adjacent to the FDJ.
claims.source: By postnatal day 2 (P2), at the peak of GN neurogenesis, the infrapyramidal blade (IPB) of the GCL had begun to form adjacent to the FDJ, and all outer niches contained abundant IPs and NSCs (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: All outer niches at P2 contained abundant IPs and NSCs.
claims.source: By postnatal day 2 (P2), at the peak of GN neurogenesis, the infrapyramidal blade (IPB) of the GCL had begun to form adjacent to the FDJ, and all outer niches contained abundant IPs and NSCs (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: Many mitotic figures were seen at P2, including Tbr2+ IPs dividing in the nascent SGZ and Tbr2+/Sox+/Pax6+ mitotic figures (transition from NSC to IP) in the FDJ.
claims.source: Many mitotic figures were seen, for example, Tbr2+ IPs dividing in the nascent SGZ (Figure 1H) and Tbr2+/Sox+/Pax6+ mitotic figures (transition from NSC to IP) in the FDJ (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1H, I.

claims.claim: By P10, the GCL displayed adult-like morphology, and the SGZ was distinct with abundant Sox9+ NSCs and Tbr2+ IPs.
claims.source: By P10, the GCL displayed adult-like morphology, and the SGZ was distinct with abundant Sox9+ NSCs and Tbr2+ IPs (Figure 1J).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1J.

claims.claim: Many Sox9+ NSCs in the SGZ at P10 exhibited a prominent single GFAP+ radial process that branched in the GCL, like 'type I' NSCs in adult hippocampus.
claims.source: Many Sox9+ NSCs in the SGZ exhibited a prominent single GFAP+ radial process that branched in the GCL (Figure 1K) like 'type I' NSCs in adult hippocampus (Nicola et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1K and citation to Nicola et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Conventional astrocyte (multipolar) proliferation was active around P10.
claims.source: Conventional astrocyte (multipolar) proliferation was also active around P10 (Figure 1L).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1L.

claims.claim: From P10 on, IP and NSC proliferation gradually decreased in outer transient niches until P21-P28, when the SGZ became the only remaining outer niche.
claims.source: From P10 on, IP and NSC proliferation gradually decreased in outer transient niches until P21-P28, when the SGZ became the only remaining outer niche (not shown).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation, though data are not shown.

claims.claim: Outer neurogenic niches in the developing DG are highly dynamic and progress by migration of IPs followed by NSCs.
claims.source: These data suggest that outer neurogenic niches in the developing DG are highly dynamic, and essentially progress by migration of IPs followed by NSCs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the temporal and spatial data presented.

claims.claim: The SGZ arises as part of the process of IP and NSC migration and contains not only IPs but also NSCs (both proliferative and quiescent) at mid-to-late embryonic periods in mice.
claims.source: The SGZ arises as part of this process, and contains not only IPs but also NSCs (both proliferative and quiescent) at mid-to-late embryonic periods in mice.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the immunolabeling data showing different progenitor types in the SGZ.

claims.claim: The primary role of IPs in formation of the DMS and other outer niches suggests that IPs are required to create a suitable niche for NSC maintenance and proliferation.
claims.source: The primary role of IPs in formation of the DMS and other outer niches further suggested that IPs are required to create a suitable niche for NSC maintenance and proliferation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference that leads to the hypothesis tested with conditional knockout experiments.

claims.claim: High Hes5GFP reporting was found in the fimbria at E14.5.
claims.source: We examined transgenic Hes5GFP reporter mice at E14.5 to visualize NSCs and Notch signaling, and found high reporting in the fimbria and mosaic Hes5GFP labeling in the DNe (Figure 2B; Basak and Taylor, 2007; Nelson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by imaging data from Hes5GFP reporter mice shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Mosaic Hes5GFP labeling was found in the DNe at E14.5.
claims.source: We examined transgenic Hes5GFP reporter mice at E14.5 to visualize NSCs and Notch signaling, and found high reporting in the fimbria and mosaic Hes5GFP labeling in the DNe (Figure 2B; Basak and Taylor, 2007; Nelson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by imaging data from Hes5GFP reporter mice shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Dll1 immunolabeling of Hes5GFP+ sections at E14.5 revealed punctate Dll1 protein in the DNe VZ and SVZ.
claims.source: Dll1 immunolabeling of Hes5GFP+ sections revealed punctate Dll1 protein in the DNe VZ and SVZ (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Within the DNe at E14.5, mosaic Hes5GFP marked subsets of mitotic Pax6high+ NSCs surrounded by punctate Dll1, and asymmetric divisions were apparent.
claims.source: Within the DNe, mosaic Hes5GFP marked subsets of mitotic Pax6high+ NSCs surrounded by punctate Dll1, and asymmetric divisions were apparent (Figure 2B1).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2B1.

claims.claim: NSCs (Hes5GFP+/Pax6+/Dll-) in the outer VZ/SVZ at E14.5 contacted Dll1+ early IPs (Hes5GFP-/Pax6+).
claims.source: NSCs (Hes5GFP+/Pax6+/Dll-) in the outer VZ/SVZ contacted Dll1+ early IPs (Hes5GFP-/Pax6+) (Figure 2B2).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2B2.

claims.claim: Some Hes5GFP+ NSCs were present in the proximal DMS at E14.5, trailing the pioneer Tbr2+ Dll1+ IPs.
claims.source: Some Hes5GFP+ NSCs were present in the proximal DMS (Figure 2B2), trailing the pioneer Tbr2+ Dll1+ IPs, and distinct from Tbr2+/Tbr1+ CRs generated in the fimbria and overlying migration routes (Figure 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2B2, 2C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Some Tbr2+ Dll1+ Hes5GFP+ pioneering IPs were observed in the proximal DMS at E14.5.
claims.source: Some Tbr2+ Dll1+ Hes5GFP+ pioneering IPs were also observed in the proximal DMS (Figure 2C), consistent with previous observations in the neocortex, likely due to rapid cell fate changes and GFP stability (Basak and Taylor, 2007; Nelson et al., 2013), although IPs due retain proliferative potential that could be further modulated.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2C and citations to previous work.

claims.claim: By E15.5, Hes5GFP+ NSCs were more abundant in the DMS, and some exhibited long leading processes.
claims.source: By E15.5, Hes5GFP+ NSCs were more abundant in the DMS, and some exhibited long leading processes (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Hes5GFP+ NSC migrations follow Dll1+ IPs.
claims.source: These data confirm that Hes5GFP+ NSC migrations follow Dll1+ IPs, and illustrate that Notch activation is maintained during NSC migrations to outer regions, a notion supported by scattered expression of Notch1, Dll1, Hes5, and Hey2 in the E15.5 DMS (Figure 2A–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the temporal and spatial expression data.

claims.claim: Notch activation is maintained during NSC migrations to outer regions.
claims.source: These data confirm that Hes5GFP+ NSC migrations follow Dll1+ IPs, and illustrate that Notch activation is maintained during NSC migrations to outer regions, a notion supported by scattered expression of Notch1, Dll1, Hes5, and Hey2 in the E15.5 DMS (Figure 2A–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by expression data and Hes5GFP reporter data.

claims.claim: Many Dll1+ and/or Dll3+ Tbr2GFP+ IPs were present throughout all transient outer migration routes and neurogenic niches including the nascent SGZ at E16.5.
claims.source: By E16.5, many Dll1+ and/or Dll3+ (not shown) Tbr2GFP+ IPs were present throughout all transient outer migration routes and neurogenic niches including the nascent SGZ (Figure 2E), although we noticed some Dll1 not associated with IPs.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: A few Dll1+/NesGFP+ NSCs were observed near the FDJ and SPNZ at E16.5.
claims.source: We examined sections from E16.5 NesGFP+ embryos and observed a few Dll1+/NesGFP+ NSCs near the FDJ and SPNZ, while Dll3+/NesGFP+ cells were rare and most likely represent residual GFP protein in IPs (Figures 2F1–4; Hodge et al., 2013; Mignone et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figures 2F1-4.

claims.claim: Dll3+/NesGFP+ cells at E16.5 were rare and most likely represent residual GFP protein in IPs.
claims.source: We examined sections from E16.5 NesGFP+ embryos and observed a few Dll1+/NesGFP+ NSCs near the FDJ and SPNZ, while Dll3+/NesGFP+ cells were rare and most likely represent residual GFP protein in IPs (Figures 2F1–4; Hodge et al., 2013; Mignone et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the known properties of the NesGFP transgene and IP differentiation.

claims.claim: Many NesGFP+ NSCs with leading processes were aligned horizontally along the SPNZ at E16.5.
claims.source: Many NesGFP+ NSCs with leading processes were aligned horizontally along the SPNZ (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: An array of NSCs located in the nascent E16.5 SGZ had their GFP-filled processes aligned radially through the underlying SPB.
claims.source: Interestingly, we also observed an array of NSCs located in the nascent E16.5 SGZ with their GFP-filled processes aligned radially through the underlying SPB (Figure 2), suggesting some NSCs have already begun transitioning into adult-like morphologies.
claims.evidence: Supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Some NSCs at E16.5 have already begun transitioning into adult-like morphologies.
claims.source: Interestingly, we also observed an array of NSCs located in the nascent E16.5 SGZ with their GFP-filled processes aligned radially through the underlying SPB (Figure 2), suggesting some NSCs have already begun transitioning into adult-like morphologies.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the morphology of NSCs observed at E16.5.

claims.claim: On P28, expression of Dll1, Lfng, Hes5, Notch1, and Notch2 were all prominently expressed in the SGZ.
claims.source: On P28, expression of Dll1, Lfng, Hes5, Notch1, and Notch2 were all prominently expressed in the SGZ, indicating a high degree of Notch signaling activity (Figure 2A, S1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Prominent expression of Dll1, Lfng, Hes5, Notch1, and Notch2 in the P28 SGZ indicates a high degree of Notch signaling activity.
claims.source: On P28, expression of Dll1, Lfng, Hes5, Notch1, and Notch2 were all prominently expressed in the SGZ, indicating a high degree of Notch signaling activity (Figure 2A, S1C).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data and knowledge of Notch signaling.

claims.claim: On P35, punctate Dll1 immunolabeling was observed on some NesGFP+ cells (NSCs or early IPs).
claims.source: On P35, punctate Dll1 immunolabeling was observed on some NesGFP+ cells (NSCs or early IPs) (Figure 2G), and on many Tbr2GFP+ IPs (some also Dll3+) (Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2G.

claims.claim: On P35, punctate Dll1 immunolabeling was observed on many Tbr2GFP+ IPs (some also Dll3+).
claims.source: On P35, punctate Dll1 immunolabeling was observed on some NesGFP+ cells (NSCs or early IPs) (Figure 2G), and on many Tbr2GFP+ IPs (some also Dll3+) (Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: During initial stages of DG development, Notch activity is highest in early DNe compared to other hippocampal and neocortical niches.
claims.source: These data indicate: 1) During initial stages of DG development, Notch activity is highest in early DNe compared to other hippocampal and neocortical niches; 2) DNe NSCs have higher Notch activity compared to IPs; 3) IPs are the primary Dll1 source during migrations through outer niches; and 4) adult IPs express Dll1 and thus maintain Notch signaling potential.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the expression and reporter data.

claims.claim: DNe NSCs have higher Notch activity compared to IPs.
claims.source: These data indicate: 1) During initial stages of DG development, Notch activity is highest in early DNe compared to other hippocampal and neocortical niches; 2) DNe NSCs have higher Notch activity compared to IPs; 3) IPs are the primary Dll1 source during migrations through outer niches; and 4) adult IPs express Dll1 and thus maintain Notch signaling potential.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on Hes1 immunolabeling and Hes5GFP reporter data.

claims.claim: IPs are the primary Dll1 source during migrations through outer niches.
claims.source: These data indicate: 1) During initial stages of DG development, Notch activity is highest in early DNe compared to other hippocampal and neocortical niches; 2) DNe NSCs have higher Notch activity compared to IPs; 3) IPs are the primary Dll1 source during migrations through outer niches; and 4) adult IPs express Dll1 and thus maintain Notch signaling potential.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on Dll1 immunolabeling data.

claims.claim: Adult IPs express Dll1 and thus maintain Notch signaling potential.
claims.source: These data indicate: 1) During initial stages of DG development, Notch activity is highest in early DNe compared to other hippocampal and neocortical niches; 2) DNe NSCs have higher Notch activity compared to IPs; 3) IPs are the primary Dll1 source during migrations through outer niches; and 4) adult IPs express Dll1 and thus maintain Notch signaling potential.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on Dll1 immunolabeling data from P35 mice.

claims.claim: High focal Notch activity and production of basally accumulating IPs occur prior to NSC migration to, and expansion in outer regions that lead to morphological changes in DG, as in neocortical gyrus formation.
claims.source: Altogether, these findings support the idea that high focal Notch activity and production of basally accumulating IPs occur prior to NSC migration to, and expansion in outer regions that lead to morphological changes in DG, as in neocortical gyrus formation (Llinares-Benadero and Borrell, 2019).
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference drawing parallels to neocortical development, supported by citation.

claims.claim: In E16.5 DNe, IPs extended dynamic processes into the VZ, presumably to interact with NSCs (GFP-).
claims.source: In E16.5 DNe, IPs extended dynamic processes into the VZ (Figure 3A, Video 1), presumably to interact with NSCs (GFP-), similar to IP→NSC interactions in the neocortical VZ (Nelson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A and Video 1.

claims.claim: IPs in the DNe SVZ withdrew VZ-processes, extended a new outwardly directed dynamically branching leading process, and began migrating into the DMS.
claims.source: Next, IPs in the DNe SVZ withdrew VZ-processes, extended a new outwardly directed dynamically branching leading process, and began migrating into the DMS (Figure 3A3, Video 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A3 and Video 1.

claims.claim: IPs exhibited coordinated migrations within the DMS, migrating along the fimbria and extending processes into, but never entering this region.
claims.source: IPs exhibited coordinated migrations within the DMS, migrating along the fimbria and extending processes into, but never entering this region (Figure 3A2, Video 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A2 and Video 1.

claims.claim: IPs migrating in the DMS contacted neighboring mitotic progenitors, including other IPs and NSCs (Tbr2GFP-).
claims.source: IPs migrating in the DMS contacted neighboring mitotic progenitors, including other IPs and NSCs (Tbr2GFP-, visible by negative contrast) (Figure 3A4-6, Video 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A4-6 and Video 1.

claims.claim: Most early IPs at E16.5 accumulated in the FDJ then continued to migrate and proliferate into the SPNZ, although a few IPs turned from the FDJ into the Hi.
claims.source: Distally, most early IPs accumulated in the FDJ then continued to migrate and proliferate into the SPNZ, although a few IPs turned from the FDJ into the Hi (Figure 3A7, Video 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A7 and Video 2.

claims.claim: By E17.5, many IP mitoses were observed in the DMS→FDJ→SPNZ, and in the inner migration route through the Hi, with inner IPs tracking towards outer IPs at the leading edge of the SPB.
claims.source: By E17.5, many IP mitoses were observed in the DMS→FDJ→SPNZ, and in the inner migration route through the Hi, with inner IPs tracking towards outer IPs at the leading edge of the SPB (Figure 3B1, Video 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3B1 and Video 2.

claims.claim: From the SPNZ at E17.5, horizontally migrating IPs turned inward to migrate radially toward the upper layer of the developing SPB, and IP migration trajectories aligned along the inner edge of the SPB upon reaching the nascent SGZ.
claims.source: From the SPNZ, horizontally migrating IPs turned inward to migrate radially toward the upper layer of the developing SPB, and IP migration trajectories aligned along the inner edge of the SPB upon reaching the nascent SGZ (Figure 3B2, Video 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3B2 and Video 2.

claims.claim: Large-scale morphogenic movements were observed in several slice culture imaging sessions resembling 'gyrification in vitro'.
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed large-scale morphogenic movements in several slice culture imaging sessions resembling 'gyrification in vitro' (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Video 2.

claims.claim: By E18.5, IP radial migrations through the SPB, and IP horizontal migrations within the SGZ were even more prominent.
claims.source: By E18.5, IP radial migrations through the SPB, and IP horizontal migrations within the SGZ were even more prominent (Figure 3C1-2, Video 3).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3C1-2 and Video 3.

claims.claim: Temporally distinct developmentally born IP cohorts migrating in different routes (SPNZ→SGZ and DMS→hilus) converged at the SGZ by E18.5.
claims.source: Moreover, temporally distinct developmentally born IP cohorts migrating in different routes (SPNZ→SGZ and DMS→hilus) converged at the SGZ (Figure 3C3, Video 3).
claims.evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 3C3 and Video 3.

claims.claim: Live-cell imaging data reveal the cellular basis for coordinated migration from the DNe into the DMS.
claims.source: These data reveal the cellular basis for coordinated migration from the DNe into the DMS, and a novel substrate for cell-cell contact dependent signaling mechanisms between migrating IPs and NSCs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the live-cell imaging findings.

claims.claim: Live-cell imaging data reveal a novel substrate for cell-cell contact dependent signaling mechanisms between migrating IPs and NSCs.
claims.source: These data reveal the cellular basis for coordinated migration from the DNe into the DMS, and a novel substrate for cell-cell contact dependent signaling mechanisms between migrating IPs and NSCs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the live-cell imaging findings showing IP-NSC contacts.

claims.claim: 2-color multiphoton live-cell imaging at E17.5 revealed IP (GFP+/RFP+) migrations and IP-IP interactions during mitosis in the DMS→FDJ→SPNZ.
claims.source: Nevertheless, 2-color multiphoton live-cell imaging revealed IP (GFP+/RFP+) migrations and IP-IP interactions during mitosis in the DMS→FDJ→SPNZ (Figure 4A–B, Video 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4A-B and Video 4.

claims.claim: 2-color imaging revealed IP interactions and migrations near developing vasculature.
claims.source: Moreover, new views of IP interactions and migrations were seen near developing vasculature (Figure 4D, Video 4), revealing similar interactions as in developing neocortex (Stubbs et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4D and Video 4.

claims.claim: Multiple live NSC mitoses (GFP-/RFP+) were observed in the FDJ, SPNZ and the nascent SGZ at E17.5, with all receiving extensive IP contacts during mitosis.
claims.source: Multiple live NSC mitoses (GFP-/RFP+) were observed in the FDJ, SPNZ and the nascent SGZ (Figure 4A) with all receiving extensive IP contacts during mitosis (Figure 4C, Video 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4A, 4C and Video 4.

claims.claim: Many NSCs and IPs had accumulated in the nascent SGZ at E17.5.
claims.source: Orthogonal views revealed many NSCs and IPs had accumulated in the nascent SGZ (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Computationally rendering two neighboring IP-NSC pairs in the SGZ showed extensive and prolonged, but likely transient contacts.
claims.source: Computationally rendering two neighboring IP-NSC pairs in the SGZ showed extensive and prolonged, but likely transient contacts (Figure 4E,F, Video 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4E, F and Video 4.

claims.claim: As one NSC extended a radial process through the overlying GCL, the paired IP elaborated its leading process aligned along the SGZ, prior to migrating after prolonged somal interactions.
claims.source: For example, in one pair (Figure 4,F1), as the NSC extended a radial process through the overlying GCL, the IP elaborated its leading process aligned along the SGZ, prior to migrating after prolonged somal interactions (Video 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4F1 and Video 4.

claims.claim: A non-migrating multipolar IP with extensive long-range processes interacted with multiple niche-localized cells, as well as directly with a neighboring mitotic NSC.
claims.source: In the other pair (Figure 4,F2), a non-migrating multipolar IP with extensive long-range processes interacted with multiple niche-localized cells, as well as directly with a neighboring mitotic NSC (Video 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4F2 and Video 4.

claims.claim: NSCs were observed migrating horizontally in the DMS.
claims.source: We also observed NSCs migrating horizontally in the DMS (Figure 4G, Video 4), and surprisingly, additional NSCs with leading processes aligned and migrating in a coordinated fashion along the Z-Y axis, in a posterior-to-anterior direction in orthogonal views of coronal slices (Figure 4H–I, Video 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4G and Video 4.

claims.claim: Additional NSCs with leading processes aligned and migrated in a coordinated fashion along the Z-Y axis, in a posterior-to-anterior direction in orthogonal views of coronal slices.
claims.source: We also observed NSCs migrating horizontally in the DMS (Figure 4G, Video 4), and surprisingly, additional NSCs with leading processes aligned and migrating in a coordinated fashion along the Z-Y axis, in a posterior-to-anterior direction in orthogonal views of coronal slices (Figure 4H–I, Video 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by 2-color live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4H-I and Video 5.

claims.claim: En face multiphoton live-cell imaging revealed laterally (horizontal) directed IP and NSC migrations through the FDJ→SPNZ route.
claims.source: This type of imaging revealed laterally (horizontal) directed IP and NSC migrations through the FDJ→SPNZ route as described, including many migrations near overlying vasculature (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by en face live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Video 5.

claims.claim: En face imaging revealed a sub-population of progenitors aligned longitudinally and migrating near the DMS→FDJ region, confirming postero-anterior migration trajectories from coronal slice imaging.
claims.source: En face imaging also revealed a sub-population of progenitors aligned longitudinally and migrating near the DMS→FDJ region (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 5), confirming postero-anterior migration trajectories from coronal slice imaging (Figure 4H–I).
claims.evidence: Supported by en face live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Video 5.

claims.claim: 2-color multiphoton live-cell imaging data reveal IPs directly interact with NSCs during migrations through transient outer neurogenic niches to establish the nascent SGZ.
claims.source: These 2-color multiphoton live-cell imaging data reveal IPs directly interact with NSCs during migrations through transient outer neurogenic niches to establish the nascent SGZ, and provide evidence for possible additional pathways of NSC and IP migration during DG formation (Li et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the 2-color live-cell imaging findings.

claims.claim: 2-color imaging provides evidence for possible additional pathways of NSC and IP migration during DG formation.
claims.source: These 2-color multiphoton live-cell imaging data reveal IPs directly interact with NSCs during migrations through transient outer neurogenic niches to establish the nascent SGZ, and provide evidence for possible additional pathways of NSC and IP migration during DG formation (Li et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the observation of longitudinal migrations.

claims.claim: By P3, most IPs migrated directly towards the SGZ through the internal DMS→FDJ→Hi route.

claims.claim: Converging IP cohorts migrated through outer niches to continually settle the SGZ.

claims.evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data from Tbr2 cKO mice shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: DG IPs exclusively generate all prenatal, postnatal, and adult-born GNs in a defined spatial and temporal developmental order.
claims.source: Overall, these experiments show that DG IPs exclusively generate all prenatal, postnatal, and adult-born GNs in a defined spatial and temporal developmental order (Figure 7F), consistent with previous cell-birthdating and chimera studies (Angevine, 1965; Martin et al., 2002).

claims.claim: DG formation captures many essential and generalizable principles applicable to other migrating progenitor systems in the developing brain, such as neocortical gyrification.
claims.source: Although the DG is a highly specialized part of the hippocampus, its formation captures many essential and generalizable principles applicable to other migrating progenitor systems in the developing brain, such as neocortical gyrification.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement of the broader implications of the findings.

claims.claim: Fundamental principles of DG formation include coordinated migration of IPs and NSCs, maintenance of outer NSCs, and de novo tissue assembly in specific regions.
claims.source: These fundamental principles include coordinated migration of IPs and NSCs, maintenance of outer NSCs, and de novo tissue assembly in specific regions.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the key findings from the study.

claims.claim: IPs interact with mitotic and migrating NSCs throughout all stages of DG development.
claims.source: Our results indicate that IPs interact with mitotic and migrating NSCs throughout all stages of DG development, revealing a new cellular substrate for actively transmitting contact-dependent signals, and show that IPs are required to pioneer the DMS and to support NSCs in outer niches.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the live-cell imaging and conditional knockout findings.

claims.claim: IPs are required to pioneer the DMS and to support NSCs in outer niches.
claims.source: Our results indicate that IPs interact with mitotic and migrating NSCs throughout all stages of DG development, revealing a new cellular substrate for actively transmitting contact-dependent signals, and show that IPs are required to pioneer the DMS and to support NSCs in outer niches.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the Tbr2 cKO experiments.

claims.claim: These data support a general role for IPs in continuously maintaining NSC pools, prominently through Delta-Notch signaling.
claims.source: Altogether, these data support a general role for IPs in continuously maintaining NSC pools, prominently through Delta-Notch signaling.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the Dll1 expression and Notch reporter data.

claims.claim: These findings support the emerging notion that coordinated migration of IPs and NSCs away from the ventricular surface, along with evolutionary modifications in Notch signaling and cell-cell contact, have played important evolutionary roles mediating cortical expansion and morphogenesis.
claims.source: These findings support the emerging notion that coordinated migration of IPs and NSCs away from the ventricular surface, along with evolutionary modifications in Notch signaling and cell-cell contact, have played important evolutionary roles mediating cortical expansion and morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement connecting the findings to broader evolutionary concepts.

claims.claim: Increased genesis of Dll1-production was linked to Notch activation in NSCs in the early DNe.
claims.source: Thus, increased genesis of Dll1-production was linked to Notch activation in NSCs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the co-expression of Dll1 and Notch signaling components in the DNe.

claims.claim: Both IP accumulation and Notch signaling are thought to contribute to initial steps in neocortical outward expansion and gyrification.
claims.source: Both IP accumulation and Notch signaling are thought to contribute to initial steps in neocortical outward expansion and gyrification (de Juan Romero et al., 2015), and we found the same in DG, summarized in Figure 8A.
claims.evidence: This draws a parallel to neocortical development, supported by citation.

claims.claim: IPs (especially processes) are the major source of Dll1 in developing neocortex.
claims.source: Likewise, IPs (especially processes) are the major source of Dll1 in developing neocortex (Nelson et al., 2013), a prominent source in the DNe, and the major source during outer DG migrations and formation.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to previous work and confirmed by the authors' data in DG.

claims.claim: High Notch activity in the DNe likely reflects the magnitude of rapid cell-fate decisions and proliferation occurring to support the burst of Dll1+/Tbr2+ IP accumulation in the outer VZ and SVZ.
claims.source: High Notch activity likely reflects the magnitude of rapid cell-fate decisions and proliferation occurring in the DNe to support the burst of Dll1+/Tbr2+ IP accumulation in the outer VZ and SVZ.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observed high Notch activity and IP accumulation.

claims.claim: Progressive switches in Notch receptor and effector composition were observed by E13.5 (loss of Notch3/Hey1, gain of Notch2/Hey2), indicating additional temporal layers of combinatorial Notch activities might contribute to regional specification and outer NSC migrations.
claims.source: By E13.5, progressive switches in Notch receptor and effector composition were observed (loss of Notch3/Hey1, gain of Notch2/Hey2) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) indicating additional temporal layers of combinatorial Notch activities might contribute to regional specification and outer NSC migrations.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observed changes in Notch component expression.

claims.claim: High combinatorial Notch signaling and increased IP genesis/accumulation in outer VZ regions distinguish the early rodent DNe from other hippocampal germinal zones and may play a role in DNe specification.
claims.source: Hence, high combinatorial Notch signaling and increased IP genesis/accumulation in outer VZ regions distinguish the early rodent DNe from other hippocampal germinal zones and may play a role in DNe specification (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the expression and immunolabeling data.

claims.claim: These results reveal surprising evolutionarily conserved factors and steps marking premigratory zones between DNe formation and neocortical expansion.
claims.source: These results reveal surprising evolutionarily conserved factors and steps marking premigratory zones between DNe formation and neocortical expansion (Llinares-Benadero and Borrell, 2019), suggesting further mechanistic insight into mouse DG development, disease, injury and repair can inform human pediatric brain malformations and treatments.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement connecting the findings to broader evolutionary and clinical implications.

claims.claim: The SGZ is seeded with embryonic NSCs that persist as a source of postnatal and adult neurogenesis.
claims.source: Together, these findings raise the possibility that the SGZ is seeded with embryonic NSCs that persist as a source of postnatal and adult neurogenesis. This interpretation is also supported by recent data showing that embryonic DNe NSCs are the origin for at least some adult DG NSCs (Berg et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of NSCs in the nascent SGZ and supported by citation to recent work.

claims.claim: The SGZ is formed even earlier than proposed previously.
claims.source: These findings suggest that the SGZ is formed even earlier than proposed previously (Nicola et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of the nascent SGZ at E16.5.

claims.claim: Dynamic cellular processes can serve as substrates for contact-dependent signals, such as integrin and Notch.
claims.source: Dynamic cellular processes can serve as substrates for contact-dependent signals, such as integrin and Notch, and are beginning to be elucidated (Betizeau et al., 2013; Kalebic et al., 2019; Nelson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a statement of general knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: IPs rapidly target dynamic processes (Dll1+) to neighboring mitotic progenitors (NSCs and IPs) during migrations and in the adult niche.
claims.source: Importantly, our new live data directly revealed that IPs rapidly target dynamic processes (Dll1+) to neighboring mitotic progenitors (NSCs and IPs) during migrations and in the adult niche.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the live-cell imaging findings.

claims.claim: The interesting switch from Notch1/3 receptors in early DNe NSCs to Notch1/2 receptors in migrating and later mature DG NSCs was analogous to the evolutionarily similar role of Notch in expansion of human outer NSCs in the neocortex.
claims.source: The interesting switch from Notch1/3 receptors in early DNe NSCs to Notch1/2 receptors in migrating and later mature DG NSCs (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1), was analogous to the evolutionarily similar role of Notch in expansion of human outer NSCs in the neocortex (Fiddes et al., 2018; Hansen et al., 2010; Suzuki et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawing parallels to human neocortical development, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Conditional genetic ablation of selected Notch components (Dll1, Notch1, Rbpj, Notch2, Lfng) demonstrates Notch activity is essential for DG development and/or adult neurogenesis.
claims.source: Although conditional genetic ablation of selected Notch components (Dll1, Notch1, Rbpj, Notch2, Lfng) demonstrates Notch activity is essential for DG development and/or adult neurogenesis (Breunig et al., 2007; Imayoshi et al., 2010; Kawaguchi et al., 2013; Semerci et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2019), phenotypic differences in knockouts along with our data indicate a more complex combinatorial and temporally regulated Notch activity network underlies this process, and that Dll1+ IPs are especially prominent and well positioned to support the bulk of Notch signaling during outer migration of outer NSCs.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to previous conditional knockout studies.

claims.claim: Phenotypic differences in Notch component knockouts along with the authors' data indicate a more complex combinatorial and temporally regulated Notch activity network underlies DG development.
claims.source: Although conditional genetic ablation of selected Notch components (Dll1, Notch1, Rbpj, Notch2, Lfng) demonstrates Notch activity is essential for DG development and/or adult neurogenesis (Breunig et al., 2007; Imayoshi et al., 2010; Kawaguchi et al., 2013; Semerci et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2019), phenotypic differences in knockouts along with our data indicate a more complex combinatorial and temporally regulated Notch activity network underlies this process, and that Dll1+ IPs are especially prominent and well positioned to support the bulk of Notch signaling during outer migration of outer NSCs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' data and comparison to previous knockout studies.

claims.claim: Dll1+ IPs are especially prominent and well positioned to support the bulk of Notch signaling during outer migration of outer NSCs.
claims.source: Although conditional genetic ablation of selected Notch components (Dll1, Notch1, Rbpj, Notch2, Lfng) demonstrates Notch activity is essential for DG development and/or adult neurogenesis (Breunig et al., 2007; Imayoshi et al., 2010; Kawaguchi et al., 2013; Semerci et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2019), phenotypic differences in knockouts along with our data indicate a more complex combinatorial and temporally regulated Notch activity network underlies this process, and that Dll1+ IPs are especially prominent and well positioned to support the bulk of Notch signaling during outer migration of outer NSCs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the authors' data.

claims.claim: IPs and their dynamic processes serve as a continuous rich Dll1 source, providing robust cell-contact mediated Notch reactivation signals targeting NSCs, maintaining their higher Notch activity and stemness in outer transient niches during DG development, similar to the neocortex.
claims.source: Altogether, our findings support the hypothesis that IPs and their dynamic processes serve as a continuous rich Dll1 source, providing robust cell-contact mediated Notch reactivation signals targeting NSCs, maintaining their higher Notch activity and stemness in outer transient niches during DG development (Figure 8B), similar to the neocortex (Kawaguchi et al., 2013; Kawaguchi et al., 2008; Mizutani et al., 2007; Nelson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings, drawing parallels to neocortex and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Adult DG IPs retain embryonic DG IP characteristics, especially long-range filopodia dynamics and cellular interactions that convey Dll1+ signals throughout the SGZ niche.
claims.source: Adult DG IPs retain embryonic DG IP characteristics, especially long-range filopodia dynamics and cellular interactions that convey Dll1+ signals throughout the SGZ niche, among other cell-contact dependent signals.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the live-cell imaging findings from adult mice.

claims.claim: The loss of IPs in Tbr2 cKO mutant mice, the major Dll1 source during migrations, largely accounts for premature NSC depletion, DG hypoplasia and adult neurogenesis termination phenotypes.
claims.source: Indeed, the loss of IPs in Tbr2 cKO mutant mice, the major Dll1 source during migrations, largely accounts for premature NSC depletion, DG hypoplasia and adult neurogenesis termination phenotypes (Figures 6 and 8C; Hodge et al., 2013; Hodge et al., 2012), similar to conditional Notch inactivation phenotypes.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Tbr2 cKO phenotype and comparison to Notch knockout phenotypes.

claims.claim: DG formation has previously been shown to require the establishment of a glial scaffolding in conjunction with Notch and Reelin signaling.
claims.source: Moreover, DG formation has previously been shown to require the establishment of a glial scaffolding in conjunction with Notch and Reelin signaling (Brunne et al., 2010; Rickmann et al., 1987; Sibbe et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: The glial scaffolding was disrupted in conditional Nes-Cre/Eomes based Tbr2 cKO mutants (active at ~E11).
claims.source: We previously found that the glial scaffolding was disrupted in conditional Nes-Cre/Eomes based Tbr2 cKO mutants (active at ~E11), whereas delaying deletion several days by using inducible-cKO Nes-CreERT2/Eomes mice and tamoxifen injection at E13.5/14.5 largely rescued the glial scaffold, although the DG anlage was still much smaller and premature NSC differentiation and depletion was still observed (Hodge et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claims.claim: Delaying Tbr2 deletion by using inducible-cKO Nes-CreERT2/Eomes mice and tamoxifen injection at E13.5/14.5 largely rescued the glial scaffold, although the DG anlage was still much smaller and premature NSC differentiation and depletion was still observed.
claims.source: We previously found that the glial scaffolding was disrupted in conditional Nes-Cre/Eomes based Tbr2 cKO mutants (active at ~E11), whereas delaying deletion several days by using inducible-cKO Nes-CreERT2/Eomes mice and tamoxifen injection at E13.5/14.5 largely rescued the glial scaffold, although the DG anlage was still much smaller and premature NSC differentiation and depletion was still observed (Hodge et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claims.claim: Pioneering Tbr2+ Dll1+ IPs serve as the initial NSC scaffolding, and are also required to help establish the later arising glial scaffolding, in conjunction with Reelin signals from overlying CRs for organizing and maintaining later arising Notch active NSCs.
claims.source: Hence our new data further indicates that pioneering Tbr2+ Dll1+ IPs serve as the initial NSC scaffolding, and are also required to help establish the later arising glial scaffolding, in conjunction with Reelin signals from overlying CRs for organizing and maintaining later arising Notch active NSCs, and continue to direct scaffolding changes as the DG matures.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the new data and previous findings.

claims.claim: In vitro studies would predict IP dynamic filopodia with high protrusion forces and increased (punctate) Dll1 loading would generate a strong in vivo Notch activation signal, even with incidental contacts.
claims.source: At the cellular level, in vitro studies (Khait et al., 2016; Shaya et al., 2017) would predict IP dynamic filopodia with high protrusion forces and increased (punctate) Dll1 loading would generate a strong in vivo Notch activation signal, even with incidental contacts (Hadjivasiliou et al., 2016; Nelson et al., 2013; Seo et al., 2016; Shaya et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on in vitro studies, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Live-cell data indicate IPs undertake more directed interactions targeting contacts to nearby mitotic cells (NSCs and IPs) delivering rapid cell-cell contacts and signals between diverse progenitors.
claims.source: However, our live-cell data indicate IPs undertake more directed interactions targeting contacts to nearby mitotic cells (NSCs and IPs) delivering rapid cell-cell contacts and signals between diverse progenitors.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the live-cell imaging findings.

claims.claim: Evolutionary increases in outer neocortical progenitor subtypes, as well as increases in progenitor process number are both linked to increased proliferation and expansion into outer brain regions.
claims.source: Evolutionary increases in outer neocortical progenitor subtypes (Betizeau et al., 2013), as well as increases in progenitor process number (Kalebic et al., 2019) are both linked to increased proliferation and expansion into outer brain regions.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: The early focal Dll1+ IP accumulation and subsequent pioneering DMS cohort likely provide a rich source of dynamic, probing processes mediating contact-dependent proliferation signals to later emerging NSCs.
claims.source: Hence, the early focal Dll1+ IP accumulation and subsequent pioneering DMS cohort likely provide a rich source of dynamic, probing processes mediating contact-dependent proliferation signals to later emerging NSCs, a continuous IP characteristic in the adult SGZ niche (Figure 8B).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' data and evolutionary concepts.

claims.claim: Notch receptors in receiving cells can distinguish between different ligands from sending cells (trans-activation), leading to different signaling modes and downstream targets and cell fates.
claims.source: At the molecular level, Notch receptors in receiving cells can distinguish between different ligands from sending cells (trans-activation), leading to different signaling modes and downstream targets and cell fates (Nandagopal et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a statement of general knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: At least canonical Dll1 and likely Jag1 activating ligands, Notch1/2/3 receptors, and Hes1/5-Hey1/2 are expressed during various stages of DG formation, suggesting different trans-activation scenarios and multiple signaling modes could mediate DNe specification, timing of progenitor migrations, and transient versus permanent niches.
claims.source: We found at least canonical Dll1 and likely Jag1 (Nelson et al., 2013) activating ligands, Notch1/2/3 receptors, and Hes1/5-Hey1/2 are expressed during various stages of DG formation (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting different trans-activation scenarios and multiple signaling modes could mediate DNe specification, timing of progenitor migrations, and transient versus permanent niches.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data and knowledge of Notch signaling.

claims.claim: Although IPs are a continuous Dll1 source, Notch receptor switching could also change trans-activating signaling modes and outcomes influencing quiescence, proliferation, maintenance, and neuron-astrocyte production during aging.
claims.source: Likewise, although our data suggest Dll1+ IPs perform a continuous NSC supportive function, and adult NSCs are derived from embryonic NSCs due to constant lineage specification (Berg et al., 2019), migrating and adult NSCs change Notch receptor composition (Notch2, this study) and become activity-dependent (Crowther and Song, 2014). These observations indicate although IPs are a continuous Dll1 source, Notch receptor switching could also change trans-activating signaling modes and outcomes influencing quiescence, proliferation, maintenance, and neuron-astrocyte production during aging.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observed Notch receptor changes and knowledge of Notch signaling.

claims.claim: Recent reports that Notch2 evolutionary modifications underlie outer migrating NSC expansion and diversity in human neocortex further underscore how subtle tuning of Notch receptor trans-activation and cis-inhibition can drive activity levels and promote progenitor diversity.
claims.source: Recent reports that Notch2 evolutionary modifications underlie outer migrating NSC expansion and diversity in human neocortex (Fiddes et al., 2018; Suzuki et al., 2018) further underscore how subtle tuning of Notch receptor trans-activation and cis-inhibition (cell autonomous ligand-receptor interaction) can drive activity levels and promote progenitor diversity.
